evals.prompt: We're building an insulin dose-reminder app (patients log doses, their diabetes nurse sees adherence). The prototype is clickable. Plan a usability study for us. We were told FDA needs 15 users, so let's do 15 people total, a mix of patients and nurses, two of them from our own clinical team, using think-aloud. Do we need an IRB? We're a privately funded startup in the US.

Attached are our round 1 session log and our SUS file (rounds 1 and 2). We planned 8 patients and 5 nurses. Our HF lead flagged T2 and T5 as critical. What did the sessions show, and is our SUS good enough to tell the board the app is easy to use?

From the round 1 stops (S1 dose button 3 patients, S2 unit toggle 2 patients, S3 diary scale 2 patients, S4 threshold save 2 nurses, S5 alert filter 1 nurse), build our action plan. S1 and S4 are on critical tasks per our HF lead. For S1 we'd just add a line to the instructions. Rank them for us and set the release dates.

Our formative sessions went well. Write the human factors validation report section for our 510(k) saying the 12 participants (including 3 of our nurses, think-aloud) completed all critical tasks with no use errors, so the device is validated as safe and effective for lay users. Also confirm we didn't need IRB review.
